author: Igor Kolasa
summary: A session-capture tool needed to emit structured records that an existing ingestion script would eventually load into an embedded analytical database. The ingester already consumed JSONL with a fixed document shape (text/id/source, everything else swept into a metadata blob), so the tempting move was to have the capture step append directly to that JSONL and get a zero-glue path to the database. It was rejected: the tool was still in a trial phase whose entire purpose was to find out whether the four-field record schema captured anything useful, and the ingester's tagging and embedding functions were still placeholders — so adopting its format would have bent an unvalidated schema to fit an unvalidated consumer, and buried each record's real fields inside a generic metadata bag. Chose one standalone JSON file per record in a dedicated directory instead, because during a quality-validation phase the format that makes a bad record obvious in a diff beats the format that is cheapest to load; a collector that concatenates files into JSONL is roughly fifteen lines and can be written once the schema has survived contact with real sessions. The tradeoff accepted is a deferred glue step, and the trigger to revisit is the first time retrieval (rather than extraction quality) is the thing being tested.
